Add a licence-name gate with an allowlist (#287)

Add tools/check-licence-names.py, its allowlist
tools/licence-names-allowlist.tsv and its tests
tools/test-check-licence-names.py. The gate lists the tracked files
with git ls-files, reads each from the work tree, splits it at line
feeds only and finds every line that holds 1 of its 3 search terms in
any ASCII letter case; its docstring names the terms. It fails on such
a line that no allowlist row claims, on a line that holds the markers
of 2 or more rows of its file, on a row whose count is lower or higher
than the number of lines it claims, and on a malformed row, which
includes a count that is not canonical ASCII decimal and a row that
repeats the path and marker of an earlier row that has 4 fields and no
carriage return, whether or not that earlier row is well formed. It
compares a count as text, so a wrong count of any length gives a
named problem. It also fails, naming the cause, when git ls-files
cannot run, fails or lists nothing, on an entry of git ls-files that
it cannot read, on an unmerged index entry, on a tracked path with a
mode other than 100644 or 100755, such as a symbolic link or a
submodule, on a tracked path that is not a regular file in the work
tree or that it cannot read, and on an allowlist that it cannot read
or that is not UTF-8. It runs git with a fixed argument list and no
shell and treats file content as data. It makes git's message and an
error's text 1 line and cuts them to 300 characters; then, in each
field that it shows, it writes a backslash and each character outside
printable ASCII once as a backslash escape. Its own 3 files are its
named exceptions; each must be tracked and must hold a matching line.
The allowlist has 1 row per kind of line in a file: path, count, owner
and marker. The gate refuses an owner other than unit-2, unit-3 or
keep; whether a row's owner is the right one is reviewed, and the
gate does not check it.

The tests build throwaway git repositories. Each refusal case that
runs the gate first runs it on the unchanged repository, which must
pass, then makes the change that it tests, to the repository or to the
gate's PATH, in 1 or more steps, such as tracking a file and then
deleting it from the work tree. It then requires exit 1, exactly 1
summary line on standard output (for --list, only path:count lines and
then a total line), and problem lines that match, 1 for 1, the cause
and any consequence that the case names with its reason, with none
left over. Each subtest makes its change to the unchanged repository.
No run of the gate may write a character outside printable ASCII. 5
cases load the gate in a separate process and call its file reader: 1
reads a regular file as a control, and 4 replace os.lstat or os.fdopen
to reach a descriptor that is not a regular file, a symbolic link that
appears after the lstat check, and a read error, once with the
system's text and once with a text of whitespace, characters outside
printable ASCII and more than 300 characters. 3 cases put a stand-in
git alone on the gate's PATH: 1 exits 3 with a message like that text,
and 2 list entries that cannot be read, to the gate and to --list.

The Agent Plugins manifest workflow runs the tests and the gate as 2
new steps, and tools/run_all_checks.sh runs them as 2 new run lines.
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of that script.
.github/squash/287.txt holds this message.

Checks a reviewer can rerun from the repository root, with their
expected outcomes:

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py

exits 0, and at the head of this change its last line is
"check-licence-names: checked: 59 lines in 35 files; 0 problem(s)".

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py --list

exits 0 and prints 1 line of path and count per file, then the line
"total: 59 lines in 35 files".

    python3 -I tools/test-check-licence-names.py
    python3 -I tools/test-run-all-checks.py

each exit 0.
